summary.title: AREX: Towards a Recursively Self-Improving Agent for Deep Research

details: Deep research answers must jointly satisfy multiple coupled constraints; simply extending a single search trajectory lets early errors persist and exhausted directions be revisited.
Key premise: a discovery–verification asymmetry — finding a jointly-satisfying answer is costly, but checking a candidate decomposes into tractable constraint-wise checks.

AREX: a recursively self-improving deep research agent with a bi-level loop — an inner research loop that gathers evidence and emits a structured provisional answer with evidence and a self-reported confidence score, and an outer loop that uses that confidence plus a recoverability judgment to Accept / Refine (carry over verified findings into a targeted new objective) / Restart, making verification the transition operator between research rounds.

A learned, self-invoked update_context tool that compresses the agent's own trajectory into a compact 'improvement state' (verified findings + citations, current/rejected candidates, unresolved constraints, next plan) rather than heuristic truncation or external summarization.

Training recipe centered on 'key steps' (decisive evidence acquisition, hypothesis rejection/redirection, context updates): key-step-only-loss supervision during mid-training and step-aware group policy optimization with bounded key-step advantage bonuses.
AREX-Turbo: dense 4B from Qwen3.5-4B backbone; AREX-Base: MoE 122B total / 10B activated from Qwen3.5-122B-A10B.
Tool interface: search, visit, update_context, finish (plus python for HLE); 128K active context window.
Inference budget: up to 300 inner-loop turns and 5 outer self-improvement rounds; final answer is the highest-confidence completed answer if none passes the threshold.

Synthetic research tasks built by picking a latent answer, attaching verifiable constraints, then abstracting constraints into indirect multi-hop descriptions; filtered for uniqueness, evidence availability, and difficulty via independent rollouts.
Teacher-model trajectories collected in the same tool environment, filtered for genuine iterative investigation, valid tool executions, evidence-reconstructable answers, and minimum confidence.
Key-step annotations from high-precision rule-based detectors, retained only for trajectories passing final-answer verification; used offline for training only.

Multi-stage agentic mid-training: browse-intensive multi-round trajectories first, then expert-reasoning data, then mixed-capability consolidation with key-step replay and academic-paper/knowledge-intensive tasks.
Key-step objective: full preceding context preserved, loss applied only to the key step (prefix, user, and tool tokens masked).

Step-aware RL: turn-level geometric-mean policy ratio with length normalization, hierarchical averaging over steps then trajectories, KL penalty to reference, advantage = group-relative outcome advantage + bounded key-step bonus gated on positive outcome reward.
Benchmarks: BrowseComp, GAIA, xbench-DeepSearch-2510, DeepSearchQA (F1), WideSearch-en (Item-F1), HLE with tools.

Baselines: frontier closed models (GPT-5.4, Opus-4.6, Gemini-3.1-Pro), open models (Kimi-K2.6, GLM-5, DeepSeek-V4 Flash/Pro, Qwen3.5 35B/122B/397B), and research agents (MiroThinker family, Tongyi-DeepResearch-30B, Quest-35B).

Inference ablations on BrowseComp: with/without autonomous context updating (ACU) crossed with with/without the outer self-improvement loop; context-update trigger/content statistics; confidence calibration histograms.

Training ablations under matched token/rollout budgets: progressive staged training vs. direct mixed training; key-step supervision vs. equal-budget random-step replay; step-aware RL vs. standard GRPO.
Appendix exploratory study on trajectory self-distillation in a simplified setting without ACU/outer loop/key-step supervision.

key_findings.finding: Recursive self-improvement contributes large gains on BrowseComp, with ACU and the outer loop being roughly additive.
key_findings.evidence: BrowseComp accuracy: 59.6 (no ACU, no outer loop), 71.4 (ACU only, +11.8), 69.8 (outer loop only, +10.2), 82.5 (full system), i.e. 22.9 points over the configuration with neither.

key_findings.finding: AREX achieves a strong capability-per-activated-parameter trade-off, with the 10B-activated MoE beating much larger backbones and rivaling frontier systems.
key_findings.evidence: AREX-Base scores 82.5 BrowseComp, 85.4 GAIA, 71.0 xbench-2510, 89.9 DeepSearchQA, 82.0 WideSearch-en (best reported), 52.4 HLE-tool, exceeding Qwen3.5-397B on all reported columns except GAIA-adjacent margins, and surpassing DeepSeek-V4-Pro on DeepSearchQA, WideSearch-en, and text-only HLE; AREX-Turbo (4B) beats Qwen3.5-35B on five of six benchmarks.

key_findings.finding: Annotated key steps remain underfit after full-trajectory supervision, and concentrating supervision on them matters more than any other training component tested.
key_findings.evidence: Average step loss is 0.232 for ordinary steps vs. 0.277 (evidence discovery), 0.298 (path rejection/redirection), and 0.300 (key context update), i.e. ~19-29% higher; replacing key-step supervision with equal-budget random-step replay drops BrowseComp from 82.5 to 74.1, the largest ablation degradation.

key_findings.finding: Autonomous context updating is used proactively as a research-state operation, not as a context-length safety valve.
key_findings.evidence: On BrowseComp, update_context is invoked in 80.3% of cases at mean 25.7K / median 25.4K active tokens versus a 128K limit (only 0.01% of updates at the limit); triggers are dominated by search-strategy revision (66.9%) and candidate rejection (13.6%), and updates most often retain next-step plans (96.4%), unresolved constraints (95.5%), and rejected candidates (81.5%).

key_findings.finding: The agent's self-reported answer-level confidence is informative enough to drive the accept/refine decision, and staged training plus step-aware RL each add measurable gains.
key_findings.evidence: With ACU, 95.9% of correct outputs land in the 90-100 confidence bin while 55.2% of errors fall below 60; ablations show 82.5 vs. 77.5 for staged versus direct mixed mid-training and 82.5 vs. 79.4 for step-aware RL versus standard GRPO.
